source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView weekly surveillance reports covering the week of 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 for influenza cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and ILI activity in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States and is the primary expected source for extractable case, death, and hospitalization records within the target time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET hospitalization surveillance data for the 2024-2025 influenza season covering the target week.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FluSurv-NET provides laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalization rates by age group and geography, directly supporting the hospitalizations target field.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state and territorial health department influenza surveillance reports published during or covering 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Subnational reports from state health departments provide locality-level data for subnational_location and locality fields not always disaggregated in national CDC reports.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS) or PAHO FluNet data for the United States covering the target week.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO/PAHO international surveillance data provides an independent cross-check on U.S. influenza activity counts and positivity rates reported by CDC.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HealthMap, ProMED, or ECDC influenza situation reports referencing United States influenza activity for the target period.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregator and international surveillance platforms provide secondary validation of case and outbreak signals without duplicating CDC primary data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definitions and surveillance methodology are required to correctly interpret count semantics (confirmed vs. suspected vs. ILI) and normalize extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing early 2024-2025 U.S. influenza season epidemiology or surveillance methods.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources provide case definition context, historical baselines, and methodological framing for interpreting surveillance counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that aggregate influenza with other respiratory viruses (RSV, COVID-19) without disaggregation, or that conflate avian/zoonotic influenza with seasonal human influenza.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Mixed respiratory virus reports or avian influenza references must be reviewed to avoid excluded disease terms entering the collection per the task acceptance contract.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC Influenza Division publishes weekly FluView reports covering ILI activity, laboratory surveillance, hospitalization rates (FluSurv-NET), and mortality data. State health departments publish complementary subnational reports. These are the highest-priority extractable sources for the target fields.
WHO FluNet, PAHO influenza surveillance bulletins, and ECDC global influenza updates include U.S. data and serve as independent validation sources against CDC primary reports.

CDC FluView Interactive dashboard, WHO FluNet open data portal, and HealthData.gov influenza datasets provide structured, queryable surveillance data that can validate extracted records from narrative reports.
Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on the 2024-2025 U.S. influenza season provide case definitions, surveillance methodology context, and baseline comparisons for interpreting extracted counts.

Reputable health news outlets (e.g., STAT News, Reuters Health, AP) and situation report aggregators (ProMED, HealthMap) may carry early influenza season signals or outbreak alerts for the United States during the target week.

source_planning_risks.risk: A source intended for validation may leak into collection if roles are not enforced during later discovery.
source_planning_risks.mitigation: Keep validation-reserved sources separate until evaluation.

source_planning_risks.risk: Cumulative, annual, newly reported, and suspected counts may be mixed across source categories.
source_planning_risks.mitigation: Require evidence quotes and count-semantics fields.
